safety.en: The park and seafront track are enjoyable, but the surrounding traffic, crossings and busy central streets needed attention.

scenery.en: Views across the city from the hills, with a very different sea view on the waterfront runs.

surface.en: Park paths + paved promenade beside the sea offer different running options.

access.en: I would choose the seafront for a beginner or an easier outing. The hills in the upper side of Barca take more effort and navigation.

experience.en: Several return visits and two very different ways to enjoy a run.

en.title: Barcelona
en.excerpt: Most of those runs have taken me up into the hills around Turó del Carmel. There are climbs, city views and plenty of other people out for a jog. Down by the sea, Barcelona offers a very different run: flatter, easier to settle into and, for most people, probably the better place to begin.
en.body:
On the hilly outing in this story, I planned to run 10km. I got lost, and the activity ended up at 16km. A slightly longer tour of the neighbourhood than intended. :)

## How I discovered the upper part of Barcelona

First time I was staying with my friend, who had just finished setting up his co-living and co-working space. Staying in that part of the city is what led me to explore the hills around Turó del Carmel with my running shoes on.

**Parc del Carmel**, (around Turó del Carmel, beside Park Güell), is a [free public park](https://wanderlog.com/place/details/536741), and I remember plenty of other joggers and a good view over Barcelona from higher up. I have returned to this side of the city for runs on more than one visit.

![Rocky ground and greenery on Turó del Carmel with Barcelona and the Mediterranean below](/assets/uploads/barcelona-hills-and-seafront/turo-del-carmel-view.jpg "The view over Barcelona from Turó del Carmel.")

Photo: [Brunnaiz / Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Vistes_des_del_Tur%C3%B3_del_Carmel.jpg), [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Resized.

**Park Güell next door is a separate visit.** Most visitors need a timed ticket, although eligible residents and some other groups can enter free. I would save its ticketed area for a walk and a look at Gaudí’s architecture, rather than choose it for a run; check the [official Park Güell access information](https://parkguell.barcelona/en/planning-your-visit/faqs) before visiting.

There was plenty of uphill running in the upper part of Barcelona. As the elevation profile below shows, I started at around 100 metres above sea level, near Parc del Carmel. As you can see, its possible to climb even more:

![Elevation profile of the Barcelona run, showing several climbs](/assets/uploads/barcelona-hills-and-seafront/elevation-profile.svg "The elevation profile from my activity. Distances along the GPX line are approximate.")

## The easier option: down by the sea

On other outings, I went down to the seafront for easier jogs. These were separate runs from the hilly activity above. **The waterfront is much flatter**, with the sea beside you and less climbing to think about. 

On the map, the blue seafront guide follows about 4+ km one way, from the Barceloneta beachfront, past Port Olímpic, Nova Icària, Bogatell and Mar Bella, to Platja de Llevant. Running that section out and back **gives you about 8-9 km.**

For a beginner, or for a day when I just wanted a straightforward run, this would be my choice. I enjoyed the hills, but the seafront seemed a better fit for most people who simply want to put on their shoes and go for a jog in Barcelona.

![The broad paved Barceloneta promenade running beside the beach and sea](/assets/uploads/barcelona-hills-and-seafront/barceloneta-promenade.jpg "The promenade beside Barceloneta beach.")

Photo: [DimiTalen / Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Promenade_and_beach,_Platja_de_la_Barceloneta,_Barcelona,_2015.jpg), [CC0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/). Resized.

## Another option: a gentler out-and-back

I also found another stretch where I could settle into a longer **out-and-back run**, with a gentle incline and more room to run than in the city centre. There were only a few pedestrian crossings, so it was easier to keep a rhythm without constantly weaving between people. This separate outing covered about 9.4 km in total.

It is the **brown route on the map**. The hills around Turó del Carmel, this gentler stretch and the blue seafront guide give me three different options, depending on the kind of run I feel like doing.

## The streets between the good bits

Running through central Barcelona is awkward. Between pedestrian crossings, tourists and traffic, I kept having to watch where I was going. At times it felt like slaloming between people rather than settling into a run.

That is the distinction I would keep in mind when choosing where to run here: **the hills for climbing and city views, the gentler out-and-back for more room to run, or the seafront for a flatter outing**. Getting between them through busy streets needs a bit more patience and attention.

## Running clubs in Barcelona

I have not made it to any Barcelona run clubs myself yet. These five options are based on published information; check the organiser’s current schedule and meeting point before joining.

### Razze Club

Founded by [Vlad Stanculescu](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/vlad-stanculescu-46002013a_if-anyone-asked-me-back-in-the-day-what-are-activity-7219324300955156482-M1r2), Razze is a lively social community known as the “spicy runners”; its regular runs are [listed as free](https://www.run-clubs.eu/blog/run-clubs-barcelona). **Saturday mornings** are the usual weekly fixture, with extra sessions, times and meeting points announced on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/razzeclub/).

### Midnight Runners Barcelona

A lively, music-led **6 km bootcamp run with exercise stops**, on **Wednesdays at 20:00**, with check-in from **19:45** at Time Out Market Barcelona. The venue has advertised the runs as **free**; check the current booking in [Heylo](https://www.heylo.com/g/de65e9eb-39f5-4144-b6c1-f2e3213846ae) before joining.

[Club website](https://www.midnightrunners.com/cities/barcelona) · [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/midnightrunnersbarcelona/) · [Venue’s free-run listing](https://www.timeout.com/time-out-market-barcelona/things-to-do/midnight-runners)

### YEPALO Sunrise Runners

A relaxed morning group for runners and walkers, split by pace, with the option of a sea dip or breakfast afterwards. Their regular Barceloneta outings are **free**, on **Wednesdays and Fridays at 07:30**, meeting outside **Buenas Migas, Plaça del Mar 1**.

[Events and signup](https://www.meetup.com/es-es/yepalo-sunrise-runners-barcelona/) · [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/yepalobcn/)

### BCN Globals Run Club

A social, beginner-friendly **5 km beach run** for locals and internationals, with time to get to know people afterwards. The current **Monday** programme meets at **19:00 at La Carioca, Plaça de Pau Vila 1**, and starts running at **19:30**; participation is **free**, with optional tips through the organiser’s booking page.

[Events and signup](https://www.meetup.com/bcnglobals/) · [Website](https://bcnglobals.com/) · [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/bcnglobals/)

### Decathlon Runners L’Illa

An all-levels training group with running technique, hills, intervals and changes of pace, rather than just a steady social jog. Sessions are **free**, with **selected Wednesdays at 19:15** listed from **Avinguda Diagonal 577**; use the [official event calendar](https://activities.decathlon.es/es-ES/actividades-deportivas/detalles/8922348) to check dates and reserve a place.

  
**PS!** **Know a club I should add, spotted outdated information, or think something here should be changed or removed?** Send me a message on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/markuskaljuste/) or [Strava](https://strava.app.link/W1a7SCITG7b), and help me keep this useful.   
  
Same applies to pictures: I lost my own Barcelona photos when I changed phones, so the photographs in this story are licensed images from other photographers. They illustrate the places, rather than documenting my runs. **If you are local and have a couple of photos of the running paths or seafront that you would be happy for me to use, I would love to add them.**
